title: A zero cohomology fraction has an eventually zero numerator
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], L and F be O_X-modules, s a global section of L, p and n nonnegative integers, and W an open of X. Use open module cohomology [def-sc-open-module-cohomology] and the additive fraction presentation [def-sc-cohomology-fraction-presentation]. If xi is in H^p(W,F tensor L^n) and its fraction [n,xi] is zero, there is b >= 0 such that the cohomology map induced by mulTensorPowSection(s,F,n,b) sends xi to zero in H^p(W,F tensor L^(n+b)). No invertibility, quasi-coherence, compactness, or injectivity of transitions is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09MR, degree-zero localization preceding the lemma; zero criterion for the fraction presentation

proof.text: Import all Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.FractionZeroTensorPower and use its existing proved private tensorSectionTransition definition and tensorSectionTransition_self, tensorSectionTransition_comp, and tensorSectionTransition_add theorems. The former two identities make the cohomology maps a DirectedSystem of additive groups. The last identifies a transition to exponent n+b with multiplication by s^b. No duplicate tensor-coherence declarations or proofs are introduced.

Map the direct sum of numerator groups to AddCommGroup.DirectLimit using DirectSum.toAddMonoid of the canonical component maps. The Mathlib identity of_f shows that every defining relation lies in its kernel; closure_le extends this to the subgroup of all relations. Descend the map with QuotientAddGroup.lift. Apply this additive map to the equality [n,xi]=0; its value on the generator is the direct-limit image of xi. Thus that direct-limit image is zero. No reverse comparison or isomorphism of quotients is required.

Apply the Mathlib theorem AddCommGroup.DirectLimit.of.zero_exact to the zero direct-limit image to get an index k >= n where the transition kills xi. Write k=n+b with Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le. The proved tensorSectionTransition_add identity removes the cast and identifies this transition with cohomology multiplication by s^b, proving the conclusion. The Lean proof checks arbitrary n, s=0, empty W, and zero groups uniformly.

lean.statement:
theorem cohomologyFraction_eventually_zero {X : Scheme.{u}} (L F : X.Modules)
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) (p : ℕ) (W : X.Opens) (n : ℕ)
    (ξ : (openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p W).obj
      (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules))
    (h : cohomologyFraction L F s p W n ξ = 0) :
    ∃ b : ℕ, (openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p W).map
      (mulTensorPowSection (homOfGlobalSection L s) F n b) ξ = 0
